query: For W–Cu metal-matrix composites used in heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications, what single intervention could increase thermal conductivity while retaining mechanical durability and irradiation resistance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an otherwise comparable W–Cu composite, defines the application conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with improved properties such as radiation resistance, thermal stability, and mechanical strength. Studies have shown that HEAs can exhibit superior properties compared to traditional alloys, including increased hardness, strength, and resistance to irradiation-induced damage. The use of HEAs as reinforcement in metal-matrix composites has also been explored, with promising results. Recent studies have investigated the effects of different processing routes, such as spark plasma sintering and selective laser melting, on the microstructure and properties of HEA-based composites.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in developing HEAs, there is still a need to improve their thermal conductivity while retaining their mechanical durability and irradiation resistance. The optimization of HEA composition and processing routes to achieve this goal remains an open question.
decision.why: Nanocrystalline refinement has been shown to improve the thermal stability and radiation resistance of HEAs. By optimizing the nanocrystalline structure of W-Cu metal-matrix composites, it may be possible to increase their thermal conductivity while retaining their mechanical durability and irradiation resistance. This approach is supported by recent studies on the development of nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys, which have demonstrated improved properties under extreme environments.
